stem: Before beginning client teaching, which assessment best addresses readiness to learn?

options.A: Ask how the client prefers to learn and whether the client feels ready to discuss the information now.
options.B: Begin teaching immediately without assessing the client's readiness or preferences.
options.C: Use the same teaching method for every client regardless of needs.
options.D: Delay all education until discharge even when the client is ready earlier.

rationale: AHRQ health-literacy guidance recommends assessing the patient's preferred learning approach and readiness to learn before or during education so teaching can be adapted appropriately.
educational_objective: Assess learning preference and readiness before providing health education.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, 3rd Edition — Tool 12
source_locator: Tool 12: assess learning style/preferences and readiness to learn
source_claim_supported: Effective patient education includes assessing how the patient learns and whether the patient is ready to learn.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
